newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran opens $600 mln Gulf dockyards. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Iran opens $600 mln Gulf dockyards. [CORRECTED 12:55 GMT]

text.p: Iran on Tuesday opened a $600 million dockyard at the mouth of the Gulf which will be used for shipbuilding and repairs, state-run Tehran radio said.

It said President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani inaugurated the shipyard 37 km west of the port city of Bandar Abbas which was built for $550 million in hard currency plus 200 billion rials ($66.7 million).
The shipyard will be used for repairs of ships of up to 70,000 tonnes and for building ships of up to 35,000 tonnes, it said.
Construction was also launched on two drydocks near Bandar Abbas to be used for ships of up to 300,000 tonnes at a cost of $700 million and 270 billion rials, it added.
Iran last year awarded a $260 million contract to build 10 cargo and passenger vessels to three state-run local firms.

The state-owned National Iranian Tanker Company awarded a contract to South Korea's Daewoo Heavy Industries Co for five 158,000-tonne oil tankers and will order five more 100,000-tonne tankers to replace its ageing fleet, Iranian and Gulf shipping sources said on Tuesday.

Iran has a commercial fleet of 77 merchant ships with a total capacity of 2.2 million tonnes, which carry half of all cargo to and from the country, in addition to its tanker fleet, according to official figures.
Tehran plans to replace 44 of the older ships with new vessels during the second Iranian five-year plan which ends in March 2000.
